To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IFN β binds to Ifnar1 in the absence of the high-affinity receptor Ifnar2.
IFN β binds to the low affinity Ifnar1 subunit of the type I IFN receptor complex, and that this interaction is distinct from that observed for IFN α and IFN ω.

IFN β binds to Ifnar1 in a unique manner and that this binding is required for IFN β to induce a specific set of genes that is distinct from the genes induced by the canonical Ifnar2-dependent pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanisms that underpin the biological actions of the IFNs and the identification of novel IFN-based therapies.
a unique mode of receptor engagement by IFNs, which has important implications for the design of future IFN based therapeutics.

the structural and functional characterization, and elucidation of the mechanism of action of a unique signaling complex formed by the interaction of the cytokine IFN β with the receptor subunit Ifnar1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IFN β – Ifnar1 signaling axis is a novel and unique mechanism of type I IFN signaling and that this interaction may have important consequences in the context of disease.
the unique mode of interaction between IFN β and the extracellular domain of the Ifnar1 receptor is responsible for the unique biological properties of IFN β.
IFN β can signal through Ifnar1 alone and this unique signaling axis leads to the induction of a novel IFN signature that is distinct from the IFN signature induced by IFN β / Ifnar2 signaling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a unique signaling axis for IFN β and that it is this signaling axis which leads to lethality during sepsis.
we have discovered a new IFN β / Ifnar1 interaction that is unique to IFN β and is not shared by other type I IFNs.
IFN β can signal via Ifnar2 or Ifnar1 and that these signaling events result in the expression of unique sets of genes that have different functional consequences for the immune system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IFN β has a unique mode of receptor engagement that is independent of Ifnar2, and that this mode of receptor engagement is critical for the pathogenesis of sepsis.
the IFN β–Ifnar1 complex is a novel signaling axis that can be exploited to modulate the immune system.

the IFN β –Ifnar1 interaction can be exploited for therapeutic purposes and that it may be possible to design IFN β agonists that selectively engage Ifnar1 and not Ifnar2, thereby circumventing the need to use IFN β in the presence of high concentrations of type I IFN receptor antagonists such as the anti-IFN α antibody Anifrolumab.
